title: A look at Tales from the Red Dragon Inn - fun, fast, and easy to learn
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fG1-74pj6A4

Daniel (@dungeondive) gives initial impressions — explicitly not a review, three scenarios into a campaign of roughly thirty — of Tales from the Red Dragon Inn, and the enthusiasm is unguarded. He came to it with no knowledge of the Red Dragon Inn card game at all; what hooked him was the cover, which he says would have made him flip his lid in fourth grade and still fills him with joy at nearly fifty.

He's careful about what it is: a cooperative tactical skirmish game, not a dungeon crawl. Play happens on poster-sized hex maps with terrain and enemies printed in place — easy to set up, though he'd have preferred enemy cards so the maps could be replayed with variety, and he doubts the thin poster stock will last. Initiative is a bag draw mixing heroes, companions and enemy groups. Attacks never miss; you roll damage on exploding dice, and surplus symbols feed an epic d6 pool you can bank for a huge hit or spend to block.

Solo gets a true Lone Wolf mode: two full turns, extra minor items, and simple companions like Auto the utility bot. He rates the documentation among the best he's met in a big box — a tutorial through chapter one plus an alphabetical reference. The one real gripe is the sheer volume of chits.

----

Daniel calls a game with this many chits "not effortless fun, but close" — saved by exceptional documentation. How much fiddliness will great rulebooks buy back for you?
